surprises.head: Winnipeg found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Boston usually allows fewer dangerous shots than most teams. Not tonight: Winnipeg’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 125 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Connor has a goal and two assists as the Jets get past the Bruins
paras: Kyle Connor scored his 20th of the season just over a minute in to open the scoring for the Jets. Morgan Geekie made it 1-1 for Boston on the power play early in the first, and Tyrel Bauer and Tanner Jeannot squared off midway through the period. Josh Morrissey restored the Jets’ lead late in the period. Fraser Minten tied it up for Boston midway through the second, but the Bruins didn’t score again. Morgan Barron put the Jets ahead for good late in the period, and Mark Scheifele sealed it into the empty net with a little over a minute left. Connor finished with a goal and two assists.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Nico Daws made 21 saves for the Jets, and Jeremy Swayman stopped 14 of 17 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Mario Ferraro had the best night of anyone. The Jets moved to 13-9-4 and climbed to fifth in the Central, while the Bruins dropped to 15-8-1, fourth in the Atlantic.
